dossier_meta.paper: 1-subdivisions, fractional chromatic number and Hall ratio
dossier_meta.statement_text: Is it true that a class $\mathcal{C}$ has bounded expansion if and only if there exists a function $f_6 : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that for every $r \in \mathbb{N}$ and every $G \in \mathcal{C} \mathbin{\triangledown} r$, $\rho(G) \leq f_6(r)$?
dossier_meta.context_text: Corollary 7 gives an analogous characterisation of bounded expansion via $\chi_f$ in shallow minors. The forward direction (bounded expansion implies bounded Hall ratio in shallow minors) is clear; the converse argument fails by Theorem 2. Proposition 1 shows a nowhere-dense class with unbounded Hall ratio, but no class with unbounded expansion and bounded Hall ratio in all shallow minors is known.
